# XML parser configured to resolve external entities (Python)

`qualor:python/xxe` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-611](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/611.html), [CWE-776](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/776.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A02:2025 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A02_2025-Security_Misconfiguration/), [A05:2021 Security Misconfiguration](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A05_2021-Security_Misconfiguration/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
XML parsers configured to load external entities or to fetch documents over the network:

- lxml's `XMLParser` (and related parsers) with `resolve_entities=True` or `no_network=False`;
- a SAX parser (`xml.sax`, also as used by `xml.dom.pulldom` and `xml.dom.minidom`) with the
  feature `feature_external_ges` turned on.

The rule looks at the configuration, whatever the document; it does not need request data.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
An XML document can declare entities that point at files or URLs (XML external entities). A parser
that resolves them puts `/etc/passwd` or the answer of an internal service into the parsed data,
which often ends up in a response or an error message. Entity expansion can also exhaust memory and
CPU ("billion laughs").
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the parser is told to resolve entities and to allow network access.

```python
from lxml import etree


def load_invoice(path):
    parser = etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=True, no_network=False)
    return etree.parse(path, parser)
```

**Compliant:** entities are not resolved and the network stays blocked.

```python
from lxml import etree


def load_invoice(path):
    parser = etree.XMLParser(resolve_entities=False)
    return etree.parse(path, parser)
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the defaults: lxml resolves only internal entities and blocks network access since 5.0, and
  Python's SAX parser skips external entities since 3.7.1.
- Set `resolve_entities=False` on lxml parsers that read untrusted documents.
- Or parse untrusted XML with `defusedxml`, which refuses entity tricks altogether.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- lxml
- `xml.sax`
- `xml.dom.pulldom`
- `xml.dom.minidom`
- defusedxml

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Options passed as a dict (`XMLParser(**opts)`) are not seen.
- `load_dtd=True`, `dtd_validation=True` and `attribute_defaults=True` load the external DTD a
  document names. The lxml FAQ advises against that for untrusted input, but validating trusted
  documents is their purpose, so they are not reported here; the hotspot rule
  [python.xxe-dtd-options](xxe-dtd-options.md) marks them, and `huge_tree=True`, for review.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/python/xxe/xxe.py`](../../../rules/python/xxe/xxe.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/python/xxe/xxe.yml`](../../../rules/python/xxe/xxe.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
